The Wales Coast Route: 870 Miles of Coastal Brilliance

Wales has 870 miles of coastline, and a motorcycle route tracing it offers extraordinary variety — from the dramatic cliffs of Pembrokeshire to the sweeping sands of the Llyn Peninsula, the industrial heritage of the south coast to the mountain-backed bays of the north. This is one of Britain's great motorcycle journeys.

Overview

The complete circuit follows the Welsh coast from Chepstow in the south-east to Queensferry in the north-east, with the interior return through mid-Wales. Allow 5-7 days for the full circuit, covering 120-170 miles per day. The route crosses two national parks (Pembrokeshire Coast and Snowdonia) and three Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

South Coast: Chepstow to Tenby (180 miles)

Start at Chepstow where the M48 crosses the Severn. The south coast passes through Cardiff, the Gower Peninsula (Britain's first AONB), and Carmarthen Bay. The Gower offers dramatic clifftop riding, and the beach at Rhossili is frequently voted Britain's best. Continue through Laugharne (Dylan Thomas country) to Tenby.

West Coast: Pembrokeshire (120 miles)

The Pembrokeshire section is the highlight for many riders. St David's, Britain's smallest city, sits at the western tip. The coastal roads wind through a landscape of cliffs, coves, and wildflower meadows. Allow a full day for this section — it deserves every minute.

Cardigan Bay: Fishguard to Barmouth (130 miles)

The A487 along Cardigan Bay offers wonderful sea views combined with mountain backdrops. Aberystwyth makes a good overnight stop — a Victorian seaside town with university-town character. The Mach Loop near Machynlleth is where RAF jets practice low-level flying — you might see fast jets below the mountain ridgeline.

The Wales Coast Route is underrated because Wales itself is underrated. Riders who do it invariably say it rivals — or exceeds — more famous coastal routes in Scotland and Cornwall.

North Coast: Barmouth to Queensferry (140 miles)

The Llyn Peninsula juts into the Irish Sea like Wales' reaching arm. The roads are quiet and the beaches are stunning. Continue through Caernarfon (Edward I's massive castle) along the Menai Strait and past Conwy to the north Wales coast. The Great Orme at Llandudno offers a spectacular cliff-top road.

The Return: Mid-Wales Interior (160 miles)

Return through the heart of Wales via the A470, the country's spine road. This passes through Snowdonia, the Cambrian Mountains, and the Brecon Beacons — adding mountain riding to your coastal circuit. The A470 from Dolgellau to Brecon is one of Wales' finest touring roads. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our Pembrokeshire Coast Motorcycle Route: Wales' Coastal Gem guide for more.

Planning Tips

  • Duration: 5-7 days for the full circuit
  • Best direction: Anticlockwise (south to north) keeps the sea on your left
  • Season: May-September for best weather. June for coastal wildflowers
  • Fuel: Plentiful in towns, but carry range awareness on remote coastal sections
keyTakeaways: An 870-mile circuit tracing the Welsh coast from Chepstow to Queensferry, with an inland return through mid-Wales.
Allow 5 to 7 days at 120 to 170 miles per day; the route crosses two national parks and three AONBs.
Pembrokeshire around St David's is the highlight for many riders and deserves a full day.
Ride anticlockwise (south to north) to keep the sea on your left.
The A470 return from Dolgellau to Brecon adds mountain riding to the coastal circuit.

faq.q: How long does the Wales Coast Route take?
faq.a: Allow 5 to 7 days for the full 870-mile circuit, covering 120 to 170 miles per day. It runs from Chepstow in the south-east to Queensferry in the north-east, with the return through the mid-Wales interior. The route crosses two national parks, Pembrokeshire Coast and Snowdonia, plus three Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty, so there is plenty to slow down for.

The Pembrokeshire section, at around 120 miles, is the highlight for many riders. St David's, Britain's smallest city, sits at the western tip, and the coastal roads wind through cliffs, coves and wildflower meadows. Allow a full day for it rather than rushing through, because the scenery and the roads both deserve the time.

Anticlockwise, from south to north, keeps the sea on your left throughout the coastal legs, giving you the best views and easier stops on the seaward side. Starting at Chepstow where the M48 crosses the Severn, you work up through the Gower, Pembrokeshire and Cardigan Bay before the dramatic north-Wales finish around the Llyn Peninsula and Caernarfon.

faq.q: What does the inland return add?
faq.a: The return through mid-Wales on the A470, the country's spine road, adds genuine mountain riding to your coastal circuit. It passes through Snowdonia, the Cambrian Mountains and the Brecon Beacons, and the stretch from Dolgellau to Brecon is one of Wales' finest touring roads. It transforms the trip from a pure coast run into a complete tour of the country.

faq.q: When is the best time to go?
faq.a: May to September offers the best weather, and June is superb for coastal wildflowers along the Pembrokeshire cliffs. Fuel is plentiful in the towns, but carry range awareness on the remote coastal sections and the Llyn Peninsula. Aberystwyth makes a good mid-trip overnight, a Victorian seaside town with plenty of character and services.
